questions.q: Before updating a production stack, a team wants to know whether the change will replace the RDS database. Which feature gives that preview without changing anything?

options.why: Wrong: it compares live resources with the template; it does not preview an update.
Wrong: it blocks updates to chosen resources; it does not show what an update would do.
Right: it lists add, modify and remove actions and shows Replacement True, False or Conditional per resource, then you execute or delete it.
Wrong: they roll back after a deploy when alarms fire; they do not preview.

questions.explain: Change sets preview an update, including replacements, before you execute it.
questions.remember: Want to see what an update will do, especially replacement → create a change set and review it before execute.
variants: Want to stop an update from ever replacing a resource → stack policy denying Update:Replace.
Want to find manual console changes → drift detection.
Want automatic rollback when error alarms fire after deploy → rollback triggers.

questions.q: The first create of a stack failed and it now shows ROLLBACK_COMPLETE. The template is fixed. What must the engineer do?

options.t: Delete the stack and create it again
options.why: Right: a stack in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE after a failed create cannot be updated.

options.t: Run UpdateStack with the fixed template
options.why: Wrong: a ROLLBACK_COMPLETE stack cannot be updated.
Wrong: that is for UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED, not for a failed create.
Wrong: termination protection blocks deletion and does not repair the stack.

questions.explain: Failed first create leaves a stack that can only be deleted.
questions.remember: ROLLBACK_COMPLETE (failed create) → read the first failure event, delete the stack, create again.
variants: UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED → fix the cause, then ContinueUpdateRollback, skipping resources if needed.
DELETE_FAILED on a bucket → empty the bucket or use Retain.
Long stack fails near the end and you want to keep what worked → preserve successfully provisioned resources.

questions.q: Someone changed a security group by hand in the console. The team must find which stack resources no longer match their templates. What should they use?

options.why: Wrong: it compares the new template with the stack, not the live resource state.
Wrong: it validates templates before deploy; it does not inspect live resources.
Wrong: it lints template syntax and best practice only.
Right: it compares actual configuration with the template and flags MODIFIED, DELETED or IN_SYNC; the AWS Config rule cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check can schedule it.

questions.explain: Drift detection finds manual changes but does not fix them.
questions.remember: Manual changes outside the template → drift detection (schedule it with a Config rule). Fix by updating the template or reverting the change.
variants: Need to see who made the change → CloudTrail.
Need to block manual edits → SCPs or permissions, not drift detection.
Need to block non-compliant templates before deploy → Hooks or cfn-guard.

questions.q: A CDK Pipelines pipeline in a tools account deploys to a production account. The deploy fails because the target cannot decrypt the artifacts. What is the fix?

options.why: Wrong: self-mutation updates the pipeline itself and has nothing to do with artifact decryption.
Right: it creates a customer-managed KMS key on the artifact bucket so other accounts can decrypt artifacts.
Wrong: that only limits CodeBuild concurrency for asset publishing.

options.t: Use a legacy bootstrap in the target
options.why: Wrong: legacy bootstrap is not supported for CDK Pipelines.

questions.explain: Cross-account deploys need a shared KMS key for the artifact bucket.
questions.remember: Pipeline deploys to other accounts and artifact decrypt fails → crossAccountKeys: true (the key costs money).
variants: Pipeline cannot assume the target roles → bootstrap the target with --trust <pipeline-account>.
Docker build fails during synth → dockerEnabledForSynth.
Same-account deploys only → crossAccountKeys can stay false.

questions.q: Developers must be able to deploy stacks without having broad rights to every resource the stacks create. What is the classic pattern?

options.why: Wrong: it removes least privilege.

options.t: Put the access keys of an admin user in the template
options.why: Wrong: secrets in templates are a security failure.

options.t: Use a CloudFormation service role and give developers CloudFormation permissions plus iam:PassRole on it
options.why: Right: CloudFormation assumes the role to make the changes, so developers need no direct resource rights.
Wrong: NoEcho only masks parameter values in output.

questions.explain: Service role plus iam:PassRole is the least-privilege deploy path.
questions.remember: Deployers without broad rights → CloudFormation service role (CDK: execution role) plus iam:PassRole; add permissions boundaries.
variants: Template creates IAM resources → acknowledge CAPABILITY_IAM or CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM.
SAM or macros in the template → CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND.
Pipeline in another account → trust and deploy roles in the target.

questions.q: A stack update changes a property that forces replacement of an RDS instance. The team wants a snapshot kept of the old instance that CloudFormation removes. Which setting does that?

options.why: Wrong: DeletionPolicy applies to stack deletion or removal from the template, not to replacement during an update.
Wrong: it only orders resource creation.
Wrong: it waits for success signals during create.
Right: it controls what happens to the old physical resource when an update replaces it; set both policies on databases and buckets.

questions.explain: UpdateReplacePolicy covers replacement; DeletionPolicy covers deletion.
questions.remember: Protect the old resource when an update replaces it → UpdateReplacePolicy; protect on delete → DeletionPolicy. Set both on stateful resources.
variants: Bucket must survive stack deletion → DeletionPolicy: Retain.
Final backup on delete for RDS or EBS → DeletionPolicy: Snapshot.
Block an update from replacing the DB at all → stack policy.

questions.q: An organization must deploy a CloudTrail and AWS Config baseline to every current and future account in all its Regions. Which approach fits?

options.t: A service-managed StackSet targeting OUs with automatic deployment
options.why: Right: AWS creates the roles, and automatic deployment adds the stack to new accounts joining the OU.

options.t: A nested stack in the management account
options.why: Wrong: a nested stack lives in one account and Region.

options.t: A single stack with cross-stack exports
options.why: Wrong: exports work only within one account and Region.

options.t: A self-managed StackSet with manual account lists
options.why: Wrong: you would create roles yourself and add each new account by hand.

questions.explain: Service-managed StackSets with auto-deployment cover new accounts in OUs.
questions.remember: Same template across many accounts and Regions including new ones → service-managed StackSet with automatic deployment on OUs.
variants: No Organizations, accounts outside it → self-managed StackSet with admin and execution roles.
Same lifecycle components inside one parent → nested stacks.
Template uses a transform such as SAM → service-managed StackSets cannot deploy it.

questions.q: A platform team wants to roll a SAM template with the AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31 transform out to many accounts using a service-managed StackSet. What is the problem?

options.t: SAM resources cannot contain IAM roles
options.why: Wrong: SAM generates IAM roles from Policies; that is not the limit.

options.t: Service-managed StackSets cannot use templates with macros or transforms
options.why: Right: the SAM transform is a macro, so the template must be turned into plain CloudFormation first.
Wrong: StackSets accept YAML and JSON.
Wrong: Lambda resources are normal CloudFormation types.

questions.explain: Service-managed StackSets reject transforms, which includes SAM.
questions.remember: SAM or any macro in a service-managed StackSet → not allowed; deploy plain CloudFormation (transformed output) instead.
variants: SAM deploy by hand → needs CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND.
Org-wide baseline with plain resources → service-managed StackSet.
Self-managed StackSet → you create the admin and execution roles yourself.

questions.q: A template creates an RDS database. The master password must never appear in the template, a parameter value or the console. Which option is best?

options.why: Wrong: NoEcho only masks display; it is not a secure store.

options.t: A Mappings section with the password per environment
options.why: Wrong: it puts the secret in the template.

options.t: A dynamic reference such as {{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}, or a secret generated with GenerateSecretString
options.why: Right: the value is resolved at deploy time and is not stored in the template.

options.t: The password in the instance user data
options.why: Wrong: user data is visible and dynamic references are not supported there.

questions.explain: Use Secrets Manager dynamic references or generated secrets.
questions.remember: Keep secrets out of templates → dynamic reference to Secrets Manager or SSM SecureString, or let Secrets Manager generate it.
variants: Plain non-secret config → SSM parameter types or {{resolve:ssm:...}}.
Latest AMI ID at deploy time → AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value<String> parameter type.
Limit: 60 dynamic references per template.

questions.q: An EC2 instance in a stack must finish installing software from user data before the stack is marked complete. Which combination does this?

options.why: Wrong: DeletionPolicy is for deletion; cfn-hup re-applies metadata on updates.
Wrong: DependsOn orders resources and cannot wait for a script.
Wrong: neither waits for success signals.

options.t: CreationPolicy with cfn-signal sent from user data
options.why: Right: the resource waits for the signal, with a Timeout and a Count; cfn-init can apply the configuration first.

questions.explain: CreationPolicy plus cfn-signal makes CloudFormation wait for real readiness.
questions.remember: Wait for software install before create completes → CreationPolicy + cfn-signal (cfn-init for config); WaitCondition is the older way.
variants: Re-run config when metadata changes → cfn-hup.
Rolling update of an Auto Scaling group → UpdatePolicy.
Lambda alias gradual update → UpdatePolicy CodeDeployLambdaAliasUpdate.

questions.q: A security team wants deployments blocked before creation when an S3 bucket is not encrypted, and also to check templates in CI. What combination fits?

options.t: A CloudFormation Hook in FAIL mode, plus cfn-guard in CI
options.why: Right: Hooks run proactively before provisioning and can block; cfn-guard shifts the check left into CI.
Wrong: Config detects after the resource exists; it does not block creation.
Wrong: it finds changes after the fact.

options.t: A stack policy on the bucket
options.why: Wrong: it controls updates to resources, not encryption rules.

questions.explain: Hooks and cfn-guard are the proactive, preventive path.
questions.remember: Block non-compliant resources before creation → Hooks (Guard rule or Lambda) in FAIL mode, cfn-guard in CI; Config is detective.
variants: Hook set to WARN → allows the deployment but warns.
cdk-nag → the same idea for CDK apps using aspects.
SCP → backstop that denies even when the template asks.

questions.q: A company has buckets and roles created by hand last year. They now want them managed as code without re-creating them. Which path fits?

options.t: Delete them and deploy a new stack
options.why: Wrong: re-creating risks data loss and downtime.

options.t: Run drift detection on a new empty stack
options.why: Wrong: drift detection only checks resources already in a stack.

options.t: Use the IaC generator to scan and build a template, then import the resources into a stack
options.why: Right: the scan generates a template, and resource import brings the existing resources in; `cdk migrate` can convert it into a CDK app.

options.t: Copy the console settings into a StackSet
options.why: Wrong: StackSets deploy templates; they do not discover resources.

questions.explain: IaC generator scan, then resource import (or cdk migrate).
questions.remember: Click-ops resources to IaC → IaC generator scan → template → resource import or cdk migrate; imports need a DeletionPolicy in the template.
variants: Move a resource between stacks → Retain, remove from stack A, import into stack B.
Existing resources into a CDK stack directly → cdk import.
Scan validity is 30 days and a template holds up to 500 resources.

questions.q: A team deploys Lambda code with AWS SAM and wants 10% of traffic on the new version for 10 minutes, with automatic rollback if the error alarm fires. What do they configure?

options.t: A Lambda function URL with a weighted alias in the console
options.why: Wrong: manual console work is not repeatable and has no alarm rollback.
Wrong: sam sync is for dev only and causes drift.

options.t: An Auto Scaling rolling update with UpdatePolicy
options.why: Wrong: that is for Auto Scaling groups, not Lambda traffic shifting.
Right: SAM publishes a version, shifts traffic through CodeDeploy, and rolls back if an alarm fires.

questions.explain: AutoPublishAlias plus DeploymentPreference gives canary releases with alarm rollback.
questions.remember: Gradual Lambda release with auto rollback → AutoPublishAlias + DeploymentPreference (canary or linear) + Alarms. CDK equivalent: LambdaDeploymentGroup.
variants: Run a test Lambda before traffic shifts → PreTraffic hook.
Increase 10% every few minutes → a Linear type such as Linear10PercentEvery2Minutes.
The first deploy needs an existing version, so add DeploymentPreference after the first deploy.

questions.q: A SAM Python function using numpy deploys fine but fails in Lambda with `Unable to import module`. Which command fixes the build?

options.why: Right: it builds inside a Lambda-like image so native dependencies match the Lambda platform and architecture.
Wrong: it runs the API locally and does not change the packaged dependencies.
Wrong: it deletes the stack and artifacts.
Wrong: it generates CI/CD config and does not rebuild dependencies.

questions.explain: Native libraries need a build matching the Lambda environment.
questions.remember: Import errors from native dependencies after deploy → sam build --use-container and check Architectures (arm64 or x86).
variants: Speed up builds → --parallel and --cached.
Test locally with a sample S3 event → sam local generate-event plus sam local invoke -e.
Need to review before executing a deploy → sam deploy --no-execute-changeset.

questions.q: A SAM function must write to one DynamoDB table in the same template. The team wants least-privilege permissions without writing IAM policies by hand. What should they use?

options.t: A managed policy such as AdministratorAccess in Policies
options.why: Wrong: far too broad.

options.t: A wildcard inline statement for dynamodb:*
options.why: Wrong: it is broader than needed and hand-written.

options.t: A SAM connector from the function to the table with Write permission
options.why: Right: SAM writes the IAM policies from a Source, Destination and Read or Write statement; a policy template such as DynamoDBCrudPolicy is the other option.
Wrong: a boundary limits the maximum permissions; it grants none.

questions.explain: Connectors and policy templates generate scoped permissions.
questions.remember: Least-privilege between serverless resources without writing IAM → SAM connectors or policy templates.
variants: Read only one bucket → S3ReadPolicy with the bucket name.
In CDK → use L2 grant methods such as table.grantReadWriteData(fn).
Enterprise accounts that require boundaries → PermissionsBoundary on generated roles.

questions.q: Developers want to change Lambda code and see it in the cloud within seconds while coding, on a personal dev stack. Which SAM command fits?

options.why: Wrong: it only uploads artifacts.
Right: it pushes code changes directly with service APIs where possible, skipping CloudFormation; use it for dev only because it causes drift.
Wrong: it checks the template; it does not deploy.
Wrong: it publishes an app to the Serverless Application Repository.

questions.explain: sam sync --watch is the fast dev loop, never for prod.
questions.remember: Seconds-level cloud feedback in dev → sam sync --watch (CDK: cdk watch or hotswap; CloudFormation: express mode).
variants: Test an HTTP endpoint on the laptop → sam local start-api.
Production release → normal sam deploy through a change set.
Clean up a dev stack and artifacts → sam delete.

questions.q: A Python team wants to define a data pipeline with loops and reusable components, and have S3 and Lambda permissions generated at least privilege. Which tool fits best?

options.t: AWS CDK with L2 constructs and grant methods
options.why: Right: CDK synthesizes CloudFormation from real code, and L2 grant* methods write resource-scoped IAM.
Wrong: it has no loops or grant helpers.
Wrong: StackSets spread a template across accounts and Regions; they are not an authoring tool.
Wrong: SAM is a serverless shorthand in YAML, not a general programming model.

questions.explain: CDK is the code-first option with built-in least privilege helpers.
questions.remember: Define infrastructure in Python or TypeScript → CDK (cdk synth makes the template). Serverless YAML with local tests → SAM.
variants: L1 constructs (Cfn*) map one-to-one and have no defaults.
Short serverless YAML expanded by a transform → SAM.
Same template to many accounts → StackSets.

questions.q: A CDK deploy to a new account fails with an error that the toolkit stack must be deployed because the stack uses assets. What should the engineer do?

options.why: Wrong: synth produces the template and does not create the toolkit stack.
Wrong: CDK v1 reached end of support on 1 June 2023.

options.t: Run `cdk bootstrap` for that account and Region, with `--trust` for a pipeline account
options.why: Right: bootstrap deploys the CDKToolkit stack with the asset S3 bucket, ECR repository and IAM roles; it is needed once per account and Region.
Wrong: it empties buckets on delete and has nothing to do with the toolkit stack.

questions.explain: Bootstrap once per account and Region before the first deploy.
questions.remember: Assets or bootstrap errors in CDK → cdk bootstrap that environment; cross-account CI/CD adds --trust.
variants: Tighten what CloudFormation can create → --cloudformation-execution-policies instead of the default AdministratorAccess.
Bootstrap version too old → re-run cdk bootstrap.
Pipeline context lookups in the target → --trust-for-lookup.

questions.q: A CDK app must deploy to dev, test and prod accounts. A developer changes the pipeline definition in code and wants it applied automatically before the app stages. Which feature does this?

options.t: The self-mutating UpdatePipeline stage of CDK Pipelines
options.why: Right: it runs cdk deploy on the pipeline stack and restarts the run with the new definition before app stages.
Wrong: hotswap skips CloudFormation for dev and does not update the pipeline.
Wrong: it deploys templates to accounts but does not rebuild a pipeline from commits.
Wrong: it generates pipelines for SAM apps, not CDK apps.

questions.explain: CDK Pipelines is self-mutating.
questions.remember: CDK app across several accounts from one pipeline → CDK Pipelines (a Stage per account with explicit env, targets bootstrapped with --trust). SAM app → sam pipeline init.
variants: Turn off self-update → selfMutation: false.
Pipeline stuck after a bad pipeline change → fix and run cdk deploy locally.
A manual gate before prod → ManualApprovalStep in pre.

questions.q: After a refactor, a CDK deploy unexpectedly replaces a production table. The code change only moved the construct into another class. What is the likely cause and rule?

options.t: The construct ID or logical ID changed, so CloudFormation sees a new resource; keep construct IDs stable
options.why: Right: a renamed or moved construct changes the logical ID, which triggers replacement.

options.t: CDK v2 always replaces stateful resources
options.why: Wrong: it does not; the ID change is the trigger.
Wrong: a missing bootstrap fails the deploy with a toolkit error instead.
Wrong: it only blocks stack deletion, not replacement.

questions.explain: Logical IDs come from construct IDs, so changing them replaces resources.
questions.remember: Unexpected CDK replacement → a construct or logical ID changed. Keep IDs stable, use overrideLogicalId, and read cdk diff before deploy.
variants: Stop replacement damage → RemovalPolicy RETAIN or SNAPSHOT, which sets DeletionPolicy and UpdateReplacePolicy.
Review changes before deploy → cdk diff or a change set.
Stack policy denying Update:Replace is the CloudFormation guard.
